source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyaya 14 (Kashyapa's boons to Kadru and Vinata; a thousand eggs and two; five hundred years in steaming jars). Told out of the CE's order: the arc opens with Parikshit and the sacrifice, then goes back to the causes (see SERIES.md, arc A02).
structure: Every episode: RECAP (≈3 s; KIT.series.recapStrip) → HOOK (one question, Sauti at the Naimisha fire; the episode title follows it: KIT.series.episodeTitle) → STORY → NEXT (a cliffhanger line, then the teaser card: KIT.series.nextTeaser).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.text: Janamejaya's fire drew the serpents down from the sky.
lines.note: RECAP. Episode 8's key image as a memory: the great fire of the sacrifice, the priests in black, serpents spiralling down into it. beats = 'fire', 'serpents'

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: But why would a mother curse her own sons?
lines.note: HOOK (Sauti at the Naimisha fire, close). In the smoke a woman's crowned shape bends over a nest of eggs. beats = 'mother', 'sons'; the title in the post

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Long ago, the sage Kashyapa had two wives: the sisters Kadru and Vinata.
lines.say: Long ago, [p:100] the sage Kashyapa had two wives: [p:150] the sisters Kadru… and Vinata.
lines.note: STORY 1. NEW PLACE: Kashyapa's hermitage in a cool blue dawn-before-sunrise, lotus pool, a banyan, Himalayan ridges. Kashyapa seated in the middle; the two sisters arrive from either side. beats = 'Kashyapa' (name), 'Kadru' (her name, olive-gold), 'Vinata' (her name, rose)

lines.text: Pleased with them, he offered each a boon.
lines.note: STORY 2. Kashyapa raises his hand in blessing; two small lights kindle in the air before the sisters. beats = 'Pleased', 'boon'

lines.speaker: kadru
lines.text: Give me a thousand sons, serpents, all equal in splendour.
lines.say: Give me a thousand sons… [p:80] serpents, [p:80] all equal in splendour.
lines.note: STORY 3 (Kadru speaks). Close on Kadru: behind her the dawn fills with a thousand small cobra hoods glinting olive-gold and green. beats = 'thousand' (the hoods multiply), 'serpents', 'splendour'

lines.speaker: vinata
lines.text: Give me only two, but greater than all of hers.
lines.say: Give me only two… [p:80] but greater than all of hers.
lines.note: STORY 4 (Vinata speaks). Close on Vinata: two great birds of light, one red, one gold, wheel behind her. beats = 'two' (two lights), 'greater', 'hers'

lines.speaker: kashyapa
lines.text: So be it. Guard them well.
lines.say: So be it. [p:150] Guard them well.
lines.note: STORY 5 (Kashyapa speaks). He blesses them both, rises and walks away into the forest with his staff. beats = 'So', 'well'

lines.text: Kadru laid a thousand eggs. Vinata laid two.
lines.say: Kadru laid a thousand eggs. [p:250] Vinata laid two.
lines.note: STORY 6. A great field of small olive eggs gleams on Kadru's side; on Vinata's, two large luminous eggs, one rose-red, one gold. beats = 'thousand' (they appear in a wave), 'eggs', 'two'

lines.text: They were kept warm in steaming jars… for five hundred years.
lines.say: They were kept warm in steaming jars… [p:150] for five hundred years.
lines.note: STORY 7. Rows of tall clay jars, steam curling; the eggs inside glow faintly through the clay. The sky wheels: sun and moon arc over again and again, seasons pass (a counter of years). beats = 'jars', 'hundred', 'years'

lines.text: Kadru's eggs hatched. Vinata's did not. And she could not wait.
lines.say: Kadru's eggs hatched. [p:200] Vinata's did not. [p:300] And she could not wait.
lines.note: NEXT 1. Kadru's jars crack: a thousand small serpents pour out, hoods rising. Vinata kneels by her two silent jars; her hand reaches for one. beats = 'hatched', 'not', 'wait' (her hand on the jar)
the teaser card, with a glimpse of episode 10: a cracked rose-red egg, a red light pouring out, the first dawn
